description: DescriptionBelow are the locations for your day trip1.Royal Palace Complex2.Gal Vihara3.sacred Quadrangle4.Minneriya National ParkBegin your adventure in Polonnaruwa, a UNESCO World Heritage Site celebrated for its rich history and archaeological marvels. As you step onto its hallowed ground, you'll be transported back in time to the days of ancient Sri Lankan kingdoms. Roam among the ancient ruins, intricately carved stone sculptures, and remarkably preserved monuments that bear witness to the island's glorious past.Our experienced guides will lead you through this open-air museum, regaling you with tales of kings and kingdoms. You'll visit the Royal Palace, where royalty once resided, the awe-inspiring Gal Vihara with its colossal Buddha statues, and the sacred Quadrangle, a spiritual center rich in history. Along the way, you'll gain a deep understanding of the art, architecture, and cultural heritage that define PolonnaruwaAfter immersing yourself in the historical wonders of Polonnaruwa, it's time for an exhilarating wildlife adventure. The Minneriya National Park, just a short drive away, promises an unforgettable Minneriya Elephant Safari. This park is renowned for its incredible gatherings of elephants, often called 'The Gathering,' where herds of these magnificent creatures come together to graze, socialize, and play.Your journey into the wild begins as you board a sturdy 4x4 safari jeep, accompanied by our experienced naturalists. They'll share their deep knowledge of the park's ecosystem and its inhabitants, ensuring you witness the awe-inspiring spectacle of Sri Lankan elephants in their natural habitat. As you watch these gentle giants up close, you'll gain a newfound appreciation for their beauty and grace.Show More

description: DescriptionBelow are the locations for your day trip1.Royal Palace2.Nissankamulla Palace3.Gal Viharaya4.Thuparama stupa5.Lankathilaka stupa6.Vatadage7.Rankoth Vehera8.Parakramabahu Statue9.Sigiriya Rock Fortress,Begin your exciting day with a pick-up from your hotel, heading towards Sigiriya.Proceed to Polonnaruwa, another ancient city steeped in history. Embark on a guided 3.5-hour tour of Polonnaruwa Ancient City, a remarkable World Heritage Site from the 12th century. Marvel at the palaces, dagobas, and temples that exemplify the brilliance of Sri Lankan historical craftsmanship. During the tour, visit key landmarks such as the Royal Palace, Nissankamulla Palace, Gal Viharaya, Thuparama stupa, Lankathilaka stupa, Vatadage, Rankoth Vehera, and Parakramabahu Statue, each holding captivating stories from the past.Climb and visit the majestic Sigiriya Rock Fortress, an ancient marvel built by King Kashyapa in the 5th century. Standing 660 feet tall, this Unesco World Heritage Site, also known as Lion's Rock or Sinhagiri, offers breathtaking views and a glimpse into Sri Lanka's rich history. Ascend the 1200 steps to reach the top and explore the well-preserved ruins of the ancient palace and water gardens. The impressive lion carving at the entrance and the innovative irrigational and archaeological technologies still in use make Sigiriya a wonder of the world. The well-designed ramparts and moats surrounding the rock are a testament to its powerful defense.As the tour concludes, return to your hotel, reflecting on the awe-inspiring historical wonders and cultural heritage experienced in Sigiriya and Polonnaruwa.Show More

Then, relax on the 1 and half hour drive to Udawalawe National Park, created in the 1970s to provide a sanctuary for wild animals displaced by the construction of the Udawalawe Reservoir on the Walawe River. Udawalawe National Park is a renowned wildlife sanctuary known for its diverse and abundant wildlife, with a special focus on its large elephant population, Now the third most visited park in Sri Lanka. The park's picturesque landscapes encompass lush grasslands, forests, and a scenic reservoir Here, you'll embark on a thrilling jeep safari. Visitors can embark on thrilling jeep safaris led by expert guides to observe elephants, leopards, birds, and other fascinating creatures in their natural habitat. Udawalawe National Park is not only a wildlife haven but also a place of conservation and environmental significance, making it a must-visit destination for nature enthusiasts and wildlife lovers.

description: DescriptionBelow are the locations for your day trip1.Galle Fort2.Maadu lake3.Turtle conservation project in Kosgoda4.Unawatuna Beach5.Stilt FishermanThe itinerary begins with a visit to Galle Fort, where guests can walk along the historic walls and take memorable photos with guidance from their tour guide. The next stop is the Madu Ganga Biodiversity Area in Balapitiya, offering an exciting mangrove boat safari. During this trip, visitors can enjoy a fish foot massage and observe various wildlife such as crocodiles, large lizards, and numerous bird species.The tour continues to the Kosgoda Sea Turtle Conservation Project, where participants can learn about and witness the conservation efforts for sea turtles. Here, the team cares for the eggs and young turtles for up to five years before releasing them back into the wild. Afterward, lunch is served at a highly-rated beachside restaurant on Unawatuna Beach, where visitors can also enjoy a relaxing walk along the coast.Following lunch, the tour heads back to Galle Fort to visit the iconic lighthouse and take more photographs. Another unique experience is offered at Koggala, where guests can try stilt fishing, a traditional method of fishing in Sri Lanka. The journey then proceeds to the Japanese Peace Pagoda in Rumassala, and concludes with a brief stop at the Sea Turtle Farm in Galle Mahamodara, further highlighting the region's efforts in sea turtle conservation.Show More

description: DescriptionBelow are the locations for your day trip1.Handunugoda Tea Factory2.Fishing at Ahangama3.Colonial city of Galle4.Kosgoda Turtle HatcheryStart your day tour with pickup from your hotel in Negombo at 6:30 AM. The first stop on your tour itinerary will be the Handunugoda Tea Factory which you will reach at approximately 9:30 AM. The Handunugoda Tea Factory reawakened the ancient Chinese tradition of creating Virgin White Tea, which is untouched by human hands during the manufacturing process. During the one-and-a-half-hour tour of the factory, see how this mysterious process takes place to create one of the top luxury teas in the world.Travel next to Ahangama to meet the stilt fishermen, who are one of the most iconic figures of Sri Lanka. Learn how they practice this unique and intricate fishing technique from a local practitioner of this ancient tradition.At approximately 12:00 PM you will stop for a lunch at your own expense in a place of your choosing, before reaching Galle at 2:00 PM. This coastal city has withstood three foreign invasions; during which time, it grew from a bustling port which was the main stop for ships travelling east, to a fortified and yet beautiful city with many monuments which have withstood the ravages of time. See the Galle Fort which is a UNESCO World Heritage Site, the Galle Lighthouse, the National Maritime Museum, the picturesque cobblestoned streets, and many more colonial remnants.Leave Galle at 3:30 PM to visit the Kosgoda Turtle Hatchery, a journey that takes approximately 1 hour. Learn about the 5 types of sea turtles that visit Sri Lanka for nesting, and how the nests are protected. You will be able to see and touch baby turtles and view some of the fully-grown turtles that are treated for injuries and ailments. Return to your hotel by 8:30 PM to complete the excursion.Show More

A bustling metropolis situated on the west coast of the island, Colombo is a fascinating mix of colonial charm, contemporary architecture, and lively local markets.Begin your day at Independence Square, a symbolic location that commemorates Sri Lanka's independence from British rule in 1948. The picturesque square features a monument and a surrounding park, providing a serene start to your exploration.Next, head to the National Museum of Colombo, where you can delve into the island's history. The museum houses a diverse collection, including artifacts from ancient kingdoms, traditional art, and exhibits on Sri Lanka's colonial past.Venture to Gangaramaya Temple, a prominent Buddhist temple that seamlessly integrates various architectural styles. The temple complex includes a museum, a library, and a sacred Bodhi tree, making it a spiritual and cultural hub.In the afternoon, immerse yourself in the vibrant chaos of Pettah Market. This bustling commercial area is a labyrinth of narrow streets filled with shops selling spices, textiles, jewelry, and an array of other goods. It's a sensory delight, and bargaining is a common practice.Explore the architectural beauty of the Old Parliament Building, a colonial-era structure with neoclassical influences. Adjacent to it stands the Colombo Lighthouse, offering a panoramic view of the city and the Indian Ocean.Lotus Tower is a prominent architectural landmark located in Colombo, the capital city of Sri Lanka. Also known as the Nelum Kuluna in Sinhala, the Lotus Tower stands as one of the tallest structures in South Asia and serves various purposes, including telecommunications, observation, and tourism.Embarking on a shopping tour in Colombo, the vibrant capital city of Sri Lanka, is an exciting and rewarding experience. description: DescriptionBelow are the locations for your day trip1.Pinnawala Elephant Orphanage2.Royal Botanical Gardens3.Temple of the Tooth in Kandy4.Kandy spice walk5.Tea factory tour6.Kandy View PointExperience the vibrant culture and natural beauty of Sri Lanka on this captivating tour from Colombo to Kandy. Your journey begins with a visit to the Pinnawala Elephant Orphanage, where you can observe and interact with orphaned elephants as they bathe and play in the river. This heartwarming experience offers a glimpse into the conservation efforts dedicated to protecting these magnificent creaturesContinue to the Temple of the Tooth in Kandy, a sacred Buddhist site that houses the relic of the tooth of the Buddha. Marvel at the intricate architecture and experience the spiritual atmosphere of this revered temple.Next, immerse yourself in the tranquility of the Royal Botanical Gardens in Peradeniya. Explore the vast collection of plants, including orchids, palms, and medicinal plants, while enjoying the peaceful ambiance of this botanical paradise.Afterwards, embark on a spice walk in Kandy, where you'll learn about the spices that are integral to Sri Lankan cuisine. Engage your senses as you smell and taste a variety of spices, gaining insight into their flavors and uses.Conclude your tour with a visit to a tea factory, where you'll learn about the process of tea production from leaf to cup. Discover the art of tea making and sample some of the finest Ceylon teaFinally, make your way to Kandy View Point, where you'll be rewarded with panoramic views of the city and its picturesque surroundings. Capture the breathtaking scenery and create lasting memories of your journey through Sri Lanka.The tour will conclude with drop-off at the same location in Colombo where you were picked up.Show More
